limitations: This is a dated, on-demand audit, not scheduled monitoring or a live Google indexing inventory.

All 116 primary public page URLs were fetched without JavaScript; 107 corresponding Lovable-host URLs were also checked. Seven Lovable pages were additionally rendered to distinguish working pages from missing HTML.
HTTP 200 confirms reachability, not Google indexing. Unknown URLs still return HTTP 200 with a not-found screen after JavaScript.

The initial live crawl checked 18 image references. A separate rendered preview check on 17 October covered 116 sitemap routes, 1,028 image instances and 300 distinct image sources, with no missing alt attributes. The 35 empty-alt instances used the decorative van icon. This is not a full visual review of every CMS image, background, responsive variant or future post. Core Web Vitals, backlinks, Meta reach and AI citations were not measured.

The foundation scanner identifies the Lovable hostname as primary, whereas source canonicals and the selected Search Console property use buyawarranty.co.uk. Its wrong-host recommendations have not been applied blindly.
Existing schema, Google Ads, payment logic, prices and article bodies were left unchanged.
Preview corrections reach the live website only after publication. Recheck both hosts afterwards; latest articles already work on the Lovable host but return generic metadata on the primary host.
A full factual review of every article remains outstanding, especially repair-cost evidence, absolute cover promises and two dealer-focused Panda Protect articles.

findings.title: Approved photo descriptions on article cards and related articles
findings.evidence: The Warranty Hub cards and related-article images used article titles even when approved featured_image_alt descriptions already existed. Seven real published article images, including the approved Mercedes EQE photo, were verified in the preview after correction.
findings.action: Reused the existing approved descriptions on featured, latest and related article images; retained title fallbacks where descriptions are absent. Generic fallback card artwork remains decorative. Also clarified the visible thumbs-up action in the Infiniti and Cadillac mascot descriptions. Photos, image URLs, article bodies, captions and schema are unchanged.
findings.next: Recheck the same article cards after authorised publication. Related articles share the approved-field fallback but were not separately exercised in the browser. Descriptive alt text improves image understanding and accessibility; Google rankings and AI citations are not guaranteed. The signed-in admin report remains unverified on external Supabase.

findings.title: Descriptive image filenames without breaking existing links
findings.evidence: Blogs 15–18 already use descriptive filenames identifying the Mercedes EQE, BMW X5, Audi Q7 and Mercedes GLE. The preview inventory recorded 300 distinct image sources; older upload IDs and remote assets need individual identity and reference checks before renaming.
findings.action: Preserved approved descriptive filenames and stable image URLs. No keyword-stuffed aliases, duplicate images or speculative renames were introduced, avoiding broken cached, shared or schema-linked image references.
findings.next: Review remaining opaque filenames individually with their actual images and all consumers before proposing a move. Keep meaningful existing filenames; filename changes alone do not establish higher rankings.

findings.title: Image delivery failures observed in the preview
findings.evidence: Six visible images finished loading with zero natural width during the rendered preview check: the UK repair-cost article hero and remote Toyota, Ford, Kia, Hyundai and Volvo logos. This is a dated browser observation, not proof of permanent failure on the published website.
findings.action: Recorded the affected pages without replacing approved imagery or changing stable external URLs. Missing alt attributes were not the cause.
findings.next: Confirm the failing image responses individually on the primary website and review existing approved local replacements before making delivery changes.

findings.title: Consistent article image descriptions and dimensions
findings.evidence: Client-side sharing tags assigned 1200 × 630 to custom images without measured dimensions. Blogs 15–18 had approved photo descriptions but sharing tags used page titles instead.
findings.action: Shared the image-metadata rules between client and prerender output. Kept verified default dimensions, omitted unverified custom dimensions and reused approved article image descriptions without changing photos, copy or schema.
findings.next: Validate default-image and custom-image metadata in the preview; recheck social previews after authorised publication. No change to article body content or warranty terms.

findings.title: Duplicate metadata inventory and footer link variants
findings.evidence: The cancellation page had two metadata entries writing to the same file; the later entry already controlled the published output. Three footer destinations omitted the canonical trailing slash.
findings.action: Removed only the overwritten cancellation entry, preserving its effective title and description. Normalised FAQ, contact and transfer footer links to their existing canonical routes.
findings.next: Run route uniqueness and coverage checks and open the footer destinations. No routes were removed and no redirects or page schemas were altered.

findings.title: Missing article metadata coverage
findings.evidence: Six sitemap articles had no build-time page-specific metadata; four published articles were missing from both the sitemap and metadata inventory.
findings.action: Added existing approved database titles, descriptions, H1s and images for ten articles, without rewriting their bodies or schemas.
findings.next: Publish, then check their returned HTML and social previews on both hosts.

findings.title: Public-page sitemap gaps
findings.evidence: Five public canonical pages and four of the 41 published articles were absent from the static sitemap.
findings.action: Added nine entries to the existing sitemap. All 41 published articles are now represented. Existing lastmod values were preserved where provenance was unknown; new entries omit lastmod.
findings.next: After publication, recheck sitemap and submit the updated XML to the selected Search Console property.

findings.title: Social-image metadata mismatch
findings.evidence: Prerender output defaulted to a 1600 × 254 PNG while advertising 1200 × 630.
findings.action: Reused the existing 1200 × 630 JPEG (about 90 KB) and removed inherited dimensions for unmeasured overrides; added page-specific image descriptions.
findings.next: Check Facebook/Meta, LinkedIn and WhatsApp previews after publication. Article-specific share-sized renditions remain a follow-up.

findings.title: Warranty-transfer canonical consistency
findings.evidence: Build-time metadata omitted the trailing slash used by the live page.
findings.action: Aligned the build-time path and new sitemap entry with /warranty-transfer/.
findings.next: Confirm one self-referencing canonical after publication.

findings.title: Missing articles should not be indexed
findings.evidence: The article-not-found branch inherited SEOHead’s indexable default.
findings.action: Added noindex to the missing-article branch only; successful article metadata remains unchanged.
findings.next: Browser-check an unknown article; hosting still needs real HTTP 404 support for genuinely absent paths.

findings.title: Primary-host publication differs from Lovable host
findings.evidence: The latest BMW X5 articles return page-specific metadata on drive-bright.lovable.app but generic homepage HTML on buyawarranty.co.uk; the primary homepage also has no initial canonical or H1.
findings.action: Kept the established primary-domain signals intact rather than redirecting search authority to the Lovable address.
findings.next: Check the primary domain’s deployment mapping and crawler delivery after the next authorised publish. Homepage content rendering needs a separate safe solution because index.html also serves private/payment fallback routes.

findings.title: Improve existing pages with Google demand
findings.evidence: Land Rover: 6,489 impressions, 39 clicks, 0.60% CTR, average position 7.93. Mercedes: 1,847 impressions, 10 clicks, 0.54% CTR, position 9.48. Main used-car page: 6,694 impressions, position 18.38.
findings.action: Prioritise clearer, evidence-led page answers and matching title/description wording on these pages, then link relevant guides to them. No keyword stuffing or invented repair prices.
findings.next: Review page-specific queries before selecting final wording; measure changes across comparable periods. Average position mixes queries and is not one keyword’s rank.

findings.title: Erroneous homepage sitemap submission
findings.evidence: The valid /sitemap.xml entry has zero errors and zero warnings; a separate submission of the homepage as a sitemap has one error. Google supplied a count, not an exact cause.
findings.action: Recorded both results without claiming the valid XML sitemap is broken.
findings.next: Remove only the erroneous homepage-as-sitemap submission after confirming it is obsolete. Keep the valid XML submission; its recorded download is 10 October.

findings.title: Review inconsistent content and AI summaries
findings.evidence: Two published consumer-path articles contain Panda Protect dealer-focused titles; llms.txt links /whats-covered and /faqs instead of canonical /what-is-covered/ and /faq/. Some summaries contain precise prices and absolute cover claims.
findings.action: Preserved existing approved article wording and recorded the inconsistencies rather than silently rewriting contractual content.
findings.next: Approve a factual content pass and explicit llms.txt update. A linked AI summary is not a guarantee of citations or AI rankings.

findings.title: Performance, links and AI/social visibility
findings.evidence: All primary HTML page fetches returned 200; that does not establish good mobile experience, backlink authority, Facebook reach or AI citations.
findings.action: Separated these unmeasured areas from observed technical defects.
findings.next: Run mobile field/lab performance checks and backlink research; measure actual social engagement and cited sources separately. SEO alone cannot guarantee social or AI platform placement.
